concept: Solana money markets: lending and borrowing (Kamino Lend, MarginFi/P0, Save, Jupiter Lend, Drift/Velocity)
summary: Solana money markets are on-chain lending and borrowing programs (Kamino Lend/klend, MarginFi/Project 0, Save/Solend, Jupiter Lend, Velocity/Drift) built on reserves or banks with LTV, liquidation threshold/penalty, utilization-driven borrow rate curves, oracle feeds (Pyth, Switchboard, Scope), elevation groups and isolated markets, and bad-debt handling. Evidence status: research claims ungated (v4 evidence gate not passed); treat as leads with cited sources. Compiled from 554 units across about 60 source hosts.

facts.text: Velocity is a perpetual-futures exchange and a money market in one Solana program. A deposit is margin and lendable at once, there is no borrow instruction (a withdrawal past zero becomes a borrow), and spot trading was removed from the program while spot markets remain for collateral and borrow-lend. Solana Compass reports the whitelist came off on 21 Sep 2026 and the relaunch was 29 Sep 2026, and that Velocity brought back perps, lending and the insurance fund but not spot trading or strategy vaults. Drift's spot borrow/lend therefore survives, as a feature of a perps venue.

DefiLlama's tvlUsd for a lending pool is the unborrowed liquidity, not total supply: Save SOL shows $7.74M against 86,112 SOL available; P0 JitoSOL $6.43M against $6.47M available; Kamino SOL/BTC SOL $19.74M against 219,590 SOL available; Jupiter's WSOL/USDC vault $84.0M against $154.8M supplied minus $69.8M borrowed. DefiLlama also lists marginfi under the slug 'project-0'. Use it to cross-check rates, not deposit totals or cap headroom.

A Kamino elevation group (eMode) is defined on the lending market with these settings: id (1 to 32; 0 means no group), ltv_pct, liquidation_threshold_pct, max_liquidation_bonus_bps, allow_new_loans, max_reserves_as_collateral and one debt_reserve. A market holds up to 32 groups. Each reserve lists up to 20 group ids it belongs to (elevation_groups: [u8; 20]) and also carries borrow_limit_outside_elevation_group, disable_usage_as_coll_outside_emode and a 32-entry borrow_limit_against_this_collateral_in_elevation_group array. The SDK type matches the program struct.

Loopscale is an order-book lender with fixed-rate, fixed-term loans (1 day to 3 months), curated Vaults and Yield Loops, and is the third-largest DefiLlama lender at $83M. Solana Compass reports that on 5 Nov 2026 Loopscale paused the protocol after a week-long attack campaign on its SOL and USDC Genesis Vaults; Loopscale said the affected vaults were made whole and no user deposits were lost, but borrowers could not repay while the pause lasted. The pause rests on that one report.

The venues are built differently. Kamino: one klend program with 50 curated markets. Jupiter Lend: a shared Liquidity layer under Earn and Vaults (Jupiter Offerbook is a separate peer-to-peer product, about $1.1M TVL). marginfi/Project 0: banks under one program plus Kamino and Jupiter Lend integration banks. Save: 205 market configs, mostly permissionless pools. Loopscale: loans filled from strategies (the adapter IDL has Loan and Strategy accounts; MadeOnSol calls it a fixed-rate order book). Across the documented Solana incidents the failing layer was the price input or its validation, not the oracle network: Mango (thin MNGO market), Solend (a single low-liquidity Saber pool feeding Switchboard) and Loopscale (unvalidated oracle account or collateral pricing logic). Current designs respond with multi-source aggregation (Kamino Scope, Jupiter Lend hops), confidence and staleness caps, TWAP/price-band guards and grade-based action gating.

In klend, utilization = borrowed / total_supply, where total_supply = available + borrowed - accumulated protocol fees - accumulated referrer fees - pending referrer fees. Kamino's published borrow APY includes a reserve-level fixed host rate that suppliers do not receive. hostFixedInterestRateBps on 2026-11-06 is 0 for SOL, 50 for USDC and 100 for JitoSOL. In klend, debt accrues at current_borrow_rate plus host_fixed_interest_rate, the fixed part is booked wholly to accumulated protocol fees, and the protocol take rate is charged only on the variable part. Each collateral-eligible Velocity spot market has its own staker-owned Insurance Fund, denominated in that asset and covering only liabilities in it, so a bad SOL borrow draws on the SOL fund and not the quote fund. The fund is fed by capped hourly settlements from the market's revenue pool (trading, liquidation and borrow fees) and by a lending-yield carveout that diverts part of deposit interest to the fund. Stakers' principal is what absorbs the debt.

Synthesis, a checklist for any 'isolated' claim: (1) liquidity: does the unit hold its own token accounts, or draw on a shared layer (Jupiter vaults share one; Kamino and Jupiter markets do not)? (2) code: does it run on a shared program (all Kamino markets use klend)? (3) oracles: one shared oracle program or per-owner feeds (Jupiter markets share one; Kamino market owners configure their own)? (4) admin: a shared multisig or a per-market owner? (5) aggregation layers: do vaults or wrappers span units? (6) loss inside the unit: its own depositors still bear its bad debt (Save, Velocity).

Elevation group structure and entry rules (klend source, master 2026-11-06): a market holds up to 32 ElevationGroup records, each with id, ltv_pct, liquidation_threshold_pct, max_liquidation_bonus_bps, allow_new_loans, max_reserves_as_collateral and exactly one debt_reserve. request_elevation_group fails if the group is already active, has new loans disabled, has no debt reserve, or the obligation holds more collateral reserves than max_reserves_as_collateral. It fails with UnhealthyElevationGroupLtv if the obligation's debt would exceed the allowed borrow value under the group's parameters.

Kamino borrowers pay the curve rate plus host_fixed_interest_rate_bps. In klend's compound_interest the interest on the fixed part goes 100% to accumulated_protocol_fees. The protocol take rate applies only to the variable part, and referrer fees come out of the protocol's take, not out of lender yield. Lenders earn nothing from the host rate, and the SDK leaves it out of supply APR. Fixed-rate reserves use a flat curve (same rate at 0% and 100%), so borrowers pay the same rate at every utilization.

Jupiter Lend standard vaults take one collateral asset and one debt asset, each vault with its own configs, caps, liquidation threshold and penalty. Vaults sit on a shared Liquidity Layer ('the shared liquidity layer for a given asset pair'), and Jupiter's COO confirmed rehypothecation. Kamino's co-founder said this means 'no isolation here and full cross contamination'. Jupiter's COO called a deleted 'zero contagion' post 'not a hundred percent correct' (The Block, 2025-12-06).

marginfi's own interest_rate.rs includes a test that its native lending rate, Kamino's supply APR and Drift's deposit rate reduce to one lender formula, borrow_rate(U) x U x (1 - cut). With a linear 40% curve and zero cuts, every venue must return 0.4 x U^2. The test multiplies Kamino's Legacy-basis figure by pace / 2 slots per second, using 2.5 slots/s (400 ms), and says that basis 'carries the wall-clock scalar for its pacing'. At today's 214 ms (4.7 slots/s) the same scalar is 2.34. The Kamino SDK defines the same scalar as rateAdjustmentFactor, 500 ms / recent slot duration.

Kamino supply APY = APY(utilization x borrow-curve APR x (1 - protocolTakeRatePct/100)); borrow APY = APY(curve APR + fixed host rate). The fixed host interest rate (used by fixed-rate reserves) is added to the borrow side only and is not part of supply APY. Kamino docs say the reserve factor (take rate) is typically 10-20% and varies by asset and market.

Kamino layers several price guards on top of the feed: fixed price bands for pegged assets (example: USDC rejected outside +/-1% of $1.00), a heuristic that rejects prices orders of magnitude off the previous update, negative prices and out-of-sequence updates, plus TWAP/EWMA smoothing meant to dilute short-lived manipulation such as flash-loan-driven updates. Oracle quality tiers (High/Medium/Low) feed into Max LTV and borrow factor, and Low tier assets may go into isolation mode; no numeric values are published.

Inference: Kamino vaults are the layer that crosses market boundaries. Allez Labs calls vaults the 'connective tissue' between pooled and isolated markets and says they rebalance across markets, so a vault depositor's exposure is the union of the reserves its curator allocates to, while a direct borrower or lender in one market is not exposed to the others. The Allez Labs post comes from a curator with an interest in the model.

Jupiter Lend vaults draw on one shared pool of liquidity per token. Its developer docs say Earn depositors and Borrow vaults 'share the same underlying pool' and that all tokens sit in the Liquidity program; Earn and Borrow never hold tokens. The user docs call the Liquidity Layer 'a unified pool of funds that every product draws from' and say utilization is measured at the token level across all vaults. The liquidity program's IDL (v0.1.9) has one TokenReserve per mint, with a single set of supply and borrow totals and one borrow rate.

Jupiter's borrow rate is set per borrowed asset in the Liquidity layer and adjusted per vault. The API exposes borrowRate = borrowRateLiquidity + borrowRateMagnifier (bps): most USDC vaults sit at 582 bps and every WSOL borrow vault at 494 bps, while JUP/USDC adds +110 (692), PST/USDC +60 (642), jlJUPUSD/USDC +150 (732) and sUSDai/USDC -100 (482). DefiLlama's adaptor composes the supply side the same way (supplyRateLiquidity + supplyRateMagnifier). Vaults that share a borrowed asset therefore show nearly the same borrow rate regardless of their collateral.

Jupiter's APIs publish no utilization field, so this figure is derived by this agent from public totals, not published by Jupiter. Summing the 21 vaults that borrow USDC gives 415.0M USDC borrowed against 474.0M USDC of Earn assets (about 87.6%; Solana Compass read roughly 93% on 31 October). Fifteen vaults borrow 1.98M SOL against 0.236M SOL in Earn plus 2.157M SOL of vault collateral (about 82.6%). Treat these as rough estimates of Liquidity-layer utilization.

Jupiter Lend's Liquidity layer has a utilisation-driven RateModel, and its @jup-ag/lend-read SDK returns borrowRate, supplyRate and lastStoredUtilization in basis points (the docs divide by 100 for percent). The pages read do not give the curve shape, the supply-rate formula or the reserve/fee percent, so these remain unverified for Lend.

Each Kamino reserve carries an interest_rate_basis flag (Legacy or TrueApr). On the Legacy basis the configured APR is spread over nominal 500 ms slots, so when real slots are shorter the wall-clock rate is higher: realized = configured x 500 ms / recent slot duration. That is x1.25 at 400 ms, and the SDK comment gives 10% -> about 16.7% at 300 ms. TrueApr reserves accrue per second, so the factor is 1. The SDK display getters multiply by rateAdjustmentFactor(); on-chain accrual uses the raw configured rate. Check the flag before comparing a Kamino curve APR to a wall-clock APR.

Do not read Kamino's worked example as a live curve. The safeguards page illustrates 'a typical stablecoin curve' with a 5% rate at 80% utilization and 150% at 95%, which gives 53.3% at 85%. The live main-market USDC curve instead charges 5.51% at 95% and reaches 36.34% only at 100%; USDG, USDT and USDS have the same shape (USDS tops out at 35.86%). At 85% the live USDC curve costs 4.93% APR. The page's claim that rates 'spike so aggressively' that borrowers must repay is therefore far gentler at the kink on live stablecoin reserves, and the steep part is the final 5% of utilization.

Jupiter Lend's program source is Instadapp's public fluid-solana-programs repo, whose README is headed Jupiter Lend Solana Program and describes a two-layer modular architecture. Jupiter's own jup-ag/jupiter-lend repo holds only integration guides, CPI reference code and Anchor IDLs. A September 2026 comparison describes the design as a Fluid shared-liquidity model, and Crypto Briefing dates the public launch to August 2025.

Jupiter Lend v2 Smart Vaults (August 2026) allow a token pair as collateral or debt, backed by a Jupiter AMM pool on the same Liquidity Layer. They are opt-in per position, so standard Earn/Borrow/Multiply positions have no AMM exposure. At launch, only correlated pairs are supported, and each vault uses one smart side. Added risks are composition shift, depeg, and extra contract surface. Health is measured on the combined USD value of both legs.

Jupiter Lend v2 Smart Vaults (August 2026) let collateral, debt or both be a token pair that doubles as Jupiter AMM liquidity on the same Liquidity Layer. They are opt-in per position, standard Earn, Borrow and Multiply positions have no AMM exposure, and at launch each vault uses one smart side and only correlated pairs are supported. Added risks are composition shift, depeg, extra contract surface, and a health ratio measured on the combined USD value of both legs.

Kamino layers four protections on its feeds. (1) Pre-validation rules reject prices orders of magnitude away from the last update, negative prices, and out-of-sequence updates. (2) TWAP and EWMA smoothing dilutes short manipulation: the docs' example is a 30-minute TWAP in which a one-block (about 400 ms) manipulation counts for under 0.02% of the average. (3) Price bands reject pegged-asset prices outside a range (example: USDC outside +/-1% of $1.00), and the protocol then falls back to the previous valid price or another provider. (4) Multi-provider consensus flags a provider that deviates

Jupiter's docs overload 'market' and 'vault'. Protocol Details defines a vault as 'a market on Jupiter Lend composed of a collateral asset and a debt asset' and also uses 'vault' for the shared lending pool of an asset pair. The Markets page uses 'market' for a curator-run group of vaults on its own program deployment. Read each 'isolated' statement against the unit it names: a single vault, an asset-pair pool or a whole market.

Solana money markets use two liquidation-test models. Kamino, Jupiter Lend and Save compare a debt-to-collateral ratio with a liquidation threshold that sits above the max-borrow LTV. marginfi (Project 0) and Velocity (ex-Drift) build a weighted health value from maintenance weights and liquidate when it reaches zero. In all five, the borrow gate (max LTV or initial weights) is stricter than the liquidation gate (liquidation threshold or maintenance weights). The gap between the two gates is the user's safety buffer.

Kamino Lend (klend) socialize-loss: the lending_market_owner, or the emergency_council if one is configured, calls it on an unrecoverable obligation. The debt is written off and each depositor's claim on the affected reserve falls in proportion to its share of total deposits. The docs call it irreversible and depositor-affecting. They say to use it only when the position is genuinely unrecoverable, all standard liquidation paths (including bad-debt liquidation) are exhausted, and the reserve has a credible recovery plan such as curator backfill or treasury.

A usable test of an 'isolated' label asks three questions and checks the program for each. Where do the funds sit: separate market or pool accounts, or one reserve per mint shared by vaults (Jupiter Lend's TokenReserve)? Which position rule is enforced: klend's elevation-group checks, MarginFi's IsolatedAccountIllegalState, Save's IsolatedTierAssetViolation, Velocity's InvalidPoolId? Is credit or liquidity separated: shared liquidity couples vaults through utilization and withdrawals even when each vault has its own LTV and ceilings.

Save (ex-Solend) docs define three per-asset parameters: Loan to value ('Borrow X% against your collateral'), Liquidation threshold ('Account health that will trigger a liquidation') and Liquidation penalty ('% of your liquidated collateral to incentivize liquidators'). The parameters page lists no numeric values; users get live numbers via 'More parameters' in the app or the reserves API.

None of the five markets credits interest account by account. klend and Save multiply a cumulative_borrow_rate and raise the cToken exchange rate (total liquidity / cToken supply). Drift moves cumulative_deposit_interest and cumulative_borrow_interest. Jupiter Lend moves a supply and a borrow exchange price. marginfi multiplies asset_share_value and liability_share_value. Interest therefore accrues only when an instruction runs the accrual routine, and a stored rate is the rate at the last accrual, not a live quote. Kamino docs say socialize-loss should be a last resort. The position must be genuinely unrecoverable and all standard liquidation paths, including the bad-debt liquidation bonus, must be exhausted. The reserve should also have a credible loss-recovery plan, with insurance or treasury/curator backfill as examples. The docs describe no on-chain backfill mechanism.

No Solana lender credits interest to accounts one by one. Each keeps a pool-level index or ratio that moves at each accrual. Kamino and Save use a cToken exchange rate (collateral supply / liquidity) plus cumulative_borrow_rate. Jupiter Lend uses supply and borrow exchange prices. Drift uses cumulative deposit and borrow interest indexes. marginfi uses asset and liability share values. Interest lands only when someone triggers an accrual (refresh, operate, deposit, borrow), a rate field read from an account is the rate as of the last accrual, and interest needs no claim transaction.

marginfi / Project 0 (docs.0.xyz) makes an account liquidatable when Maintenance health drops below zero, using maintenance weights: asset weights below 1.0 discount collateral, liability weights at or above 1.0 inflate debt. The initial-weight check for new borrows is stricter than the maintenance check.

marginfi (Project 0) computes health as the sum of asset value x asset weight minus the sum of liability value x liability weight. It prices assets at the low end and liabilities at the high end of the oracle confidence band. Initial weights gate new borrows and withdrawals. Maintenance weights decide liquidation: an account is liquidatable when maintenance health is below zero. The docs define a pair's effective LTV as asset weight / liability weight. The app's LTV uses initial weights, and its health display uses maintenance weights.

MarginFi eMode and Kamino elevation groups both raise LTV for correlated pairs but constrain the account differently. MarginFi raises a collateral's asset weight when it backs a specific paired borrow, and reconciles an account's eMode as the lowest benefit across all its liabilities, so one extra non-eMode borrow removes the benefit; the README suggests splitting positions across accounts. Kamino instead limits a group member to one debt_reserve and reverts to per-reserve parameters when the obligation leaves the group.

At release 1.12.3 (2025-10-02), klend enforced the tiers in validate_obligation_asset_tiers and failed with IsolatedAssetTierViolation when an obligation held: more than one IsolatedCollateral deposit; more than one IsolatedDebt borrow; an isolated deposit next to any other deposit; an isolated borrow next to any other borrow; an isolated deposit together with an isolated borrow; an IsolatedDebt asset as collateral; or an IsolatedCollateral asset as a borrow. Reserve validation also forced LTV and liquidation threshold to 0 for IsolatedDebt reserves and borrow_limit to 0 for IsolatedCollateral

Kamino: GET /kamino-market/{market}/reserves/metrics for APYs and totals (it has no limits), and GET /kamino-market/reserves/account-data?markets={market} for base64 reserve accounts that klend-sdk's Reserve.decode turns into depositLimit, borrowLimit, net-flow caps and the utilization guard. Velocity spot-bankruptcy waterfall (Solana Compass says Drift's exchange was rebuilt as Velocity): first the bad-debt market's own revenue pool, then that market's Insurance Fund vault (at least 1 token always stays), then the residual is socialized by lowering the market's deposit-interest index, a pro-rata haircut to every lender in that market, with the index never falling below 1. Nothing is socialized until every tranche is exhausted. Perp bankruptcies must be resolved before spot ones because both draw on the same quote Insurance Fund vault.

Kamino Lend prices reserves through Scope, Kamino's own on-chain aggregator. Scope copies prices from other oracle accounts into one feed of up to 512 entries and publishes a price only if it passes preset rules. Kamino's docs name Chainlink Data Streams and Pyth Pro as the two providers, and say Scope falls back to the next-best source when a feed goes stale, deviates or fails validation. Project 0's docs independently describe a Scope entry as a slot in a Scope OraclePrices account of 512 entries that carries no confidence interval.

Who may trigger bad-debt handling differs. Kamino: only the lending_market_owner or emergency_council, a discretionary call. marginfi: the group admin or risk_admin, unless the bank sets PERMISSIONLESS_BAD_DEBT_SETTLEMENT_FLAG, in which case any signer can call; non-admin callers also pass a circuit-breaker price gate, and durable-nonce transactions, open flashloans and accounts in receivership are rejected. Velocity: anyone, gated by a solvency flag that only the cold-admin key can flip and that is kept separate from withdrawal pauses.

A Code4rena contest on Jupiter Lend (report dated 2026-07-11) rated M-01 medium: a debt-per-collateral cap of 1e26 in liquidate.rs and operate.rs sits above the safe tick-ratio bound. In an extreme debt/collateral window get_ticks_from_oracle_price then reverts with LibraryTickRatioOutOfBounds, which blocks liquidation and freezes the vault when liquidation matters most, letting bad debt accumulate. Low finding L-05 notes deterministic liquidation reverts for particular debt amounts. I did not verify whether the fixes shipped.

Rates stored on-chain are APRs and APY is a display or SDK conversion: Kamino's SDK wraps calculateAPYFromAPR around the APR, Save's integration-guide formulas are simple rates with no compounding step, and marginfi accrues simple interest per interval. When comparing protocols, check whether a UI figure is APR or APY; Jupiter Lend's analytics page labels the same value APYs in prose and Apr in code.

Chitra's autodeleveraging paper treats ADL as a last-resort loss-socialization mechanism for perpetual venues and proves a trilemma: no policy satisfies solvency, revenue and fairness at once. Its empirical case is Hyperliquid on Oct 10 2025 (ADL closed $2.1B of positions in 12 minutes). The bibliography cites Drift's ADL code and insurance fund, but the paper models perps venues, not lending pools. Velocity's perp residual instead goes to a one-time funding-rate bump.

Drift said its Insurance Fund was not touched because the protocol was paused before liquidation or bankruptcy losses were finalized, that IF stakers can withdraw once the protocol is restored, and that fund assets would help support the restart. An insurance fund exists to absorb shortfalls from liquidation and bankruptcy, so a theft that drains the pool bypasses that waterfall.

Kamino Lend prices reserves through Scope, its in-house aggregator. Per Kamino's current docs, Scope takes pull-based prices from Chainlink Data Streams and Pyth Pro, checks each price (staleness, deviation, cross-provider consistency), publishes only prices that pass to one on-chain account, and falls back to the next-best source when a feed goes stale, deviates or fails validation. All of this is Kamino's own description; no numeric thresholds are given on the security page.

Solend USDH incident, 2 November 2022: Solend reported 'an oracle attack on USDH' that left about $1.26M of bad debt in its Stable, Coin98 and Kamino isolated pools. As of November 2025, marginfi's guide and the Project 0 docs both say handle_bankruptcy had never been executed in the main pool. The docs add that almost all bankruptcies occur in the Arena, where riskier assets see extreme volatility. They name three causes: liquidators not running properly (for example during congestion), an asset too illiquid to clear safely, and a price change faster than liquidators can respond.

MarginFi keeps the tier in each Bank's config (BankConfig.risk_tier, read as bank.config.risk_tier) beside operational_state. Jupiter Lend's Statistics page lists each vault's borrow and withdrawal ceilings, and the liquidity program accounts (TokenReserve, UserBorrowPosition, UserSupplyPosition) hold them onchain. Velocity's borrow and lend page shows the live pool list because pools are admin-set onchain state.

Until handle_bankruptcy runs, a marginfi loss is real but unbooked. The guide says the remaining depositors can never withdraw their full balance, and the last few to withdraw find too little left, in proportion to the bankrupt users' liabilities. The shortfall therefore lands on the slowest exiters, not pro rata. When a bankrupt user has several liabilities, the liquidator chooses which stay on the books, so the liquidator effectively chooses which banks absorb the bad debt.

Jupiter Lend utilization = (borrow_interest_free + borrow_with_interest x borrow_exchange_price) / (supply_interest_free + supply_with_interest x supply_exchange_price), in basis points; interest-free balances come from flash loans. Certora's audit found the division ran on rounded values (M-06, medium, fixed) and recommended scaling both sides first. A borrow reverts with MaxUtilizationReached when utilization after the operation exceeds the token's configurable max_utilization, and Jupiter's docs say immediate borrowable liquidity is capped by the asset's maximum utilization.

Solana Compass's Drift page says Velocity stopped new deposits and sign-ups on 31 October 2026 while withdrawals and open trades kept working. I found no second source, so the cause and duration are unknown.

Kamino's Scope is an open-source Solana program that copies prices from several oracle accounts into one price feed. Per Kamino's docs, it takes prices from Chainlink Data Streams and Pyth Pro, checks each against preset rules (staleness, deviation, cross-provider consistency), selects the best valid price, and publishes it to one account that Kamino's lending and vault programs read. When a provider's feed goes stale, deviates or fails a check, Scope falls back to the next-best source. One feed holds at most 512 prices. Solend's ForgiveDebt (process_forgive_debt in the Solend/Save token-lending program) follows the same write-off design as Kamino's socialize-loss. Jupiter Lend's liquidation penalty is set per vault and charged only on the portion actually liquidated (docs example: a 1% penalty gives the liquidator an extra $1 per $100 of collateral sold). The docs give no concrete LT, LML or penalty numbers; developers read liquidationThreshold and liquidationPenalty from the vault config. Positions are grouped into ticks with 0.15% spacing and a crossed tick is liquidated in one transaction.

Kamino computes health across the whole obligation. For each deposit it adds market value x liquidationThresholdPct to unhealthy_borrow_value. For each borrow it adds market value x borrowFactorPct to borrow_factor_adjusted_debt_value. A position becomes liquidatable when borrow_factor_adjusted_debt_value >= unhealthy_borrow_value, so equality counts. Current LTV is the adjusted debt divided by deposited value. A borrow factor above 100% therefore pushes Current LTV above the plain debt-to-collateral ratio.

Kamino liquidation bonus is computed in bps as bonus = max(minLiquidationBonusBps, currentLTV - liquidationLTV), then capped at maxLiquidationBonusBps, then capped at (10000 - currentLTV) so the liquidator never takes more than remaining equity. Worked example (2% min, 8% max, 75% liquidation LTV): 2% at 75-77% LTV, 5% at 80%, 8% from 83%, 4% at 96%, 1% at 99%.

Drift accrues through two cumulative indexes per spot market. The borrow index grows by index x borrow_rate x elapsed seconds / ONE_YEAR (31,536,000) / 1e6, plus a 1-unit round-up. The deposit index grows by the same product x utilization, before the insurance-fund cut. No interest accrues at zero utilization, and borrows with no deposits are priced at 100% utilization. Compounding comes only from repeated updates. min_borrow_rate is stored in units of 0.5% in the SDK (minBorrowRate x PERCENTAGE_PRECISION / 200).

Save's program stores borrow rates as u8 percents, so it encodes rates above 255% as sentinel values. When optimal_borrow_rate equals max_borrow_rate and utilization is at or above the optimum, current_borrow_rate decodes max_borrow_rate 251, 252, 253, 254, 255, 250, 249, 248, 247 as 300%, 350%, 400%, 500%, 600%, 1000%, 1500%, 2000%, 2500%. The integration-guide calculateBorrowAPY divides maxBorrowRate by 100 and does not decode them, so a copied snippet reports 247%-255% where the program charges 300%-2500%.

Save (ex-Solend) parameterises each reserve with three rate points: min borrow APR at 0% utilization, optimal borrow APR at the optimal utilization, and max borrow APR at 100%. The integration-guide code is linear in each leg: below optimal, f = U/U_opt and BorrowAPY = minRate + f x (optimalRate - minRate); above, f = (U - U_opt)/(1 - U_opt) and BorrowAPY = optimalRate + f x (maxRate - optimalRate). Utilization is borrowed / (available + borrowed); config rates are stored in percent.

On each refresh klend multiplies cumulative_borrow_rate by approximate_compounded_interest(curve rate + host rate). For 0 to 4 elapsed accrual units the result is exact. Kamino's liquidation settings aim to clear positions before they turn into bad debt. The default close factor is 25%, rising to 100% above a market insolvency-risk threshold of about 95% LTV. The kinked curve exists to keep utilization away from 100%, where every deposit is lent out and lenders cannot withdraw. Kamino says its model makes 100% utilization economically unsustainable and that 100% causes no loss of funds but blocks withdrawals. Do not copy the worked examples on Kamino's elevation-group page as a valid configuration. Its stablecoin example has borrowers deposit USDC, USDT and USDS and borrow USDC inside one group, and its SOL+LST example lets SOL be both collateral and the debt reserve. The program rejects a group's debt_reserve as collateral with ElevationGroupDebtReserveAsCollateral ('The elevation group's debt reserve cannot be used as a collateral reserve') at deposit and refresh time.

Inside a Kamino elevation group the program allows only the group's debt_reserve as a borrow and rejects that same reserve as collateral (ElevationGroupDebtReserveAsCollateral). Every collateral reserve must list the group id in its elevation_groups array (InconsistentElevationGroup), per-group caps apply through borrow_limit_against_this_collateral_in_elevation_group, and the borrow factor is forced to 1.0 (Reserve::borrow_factor_f returns ONE for group members). So the group trades the reserve's risk weights for a single-debt, capped-collateral structure.

Two per-reserve caps bound how much risk elevation groups and group-less borrowing can take. borrow_limit_against_this_collateral_in_elevation_group[group_id - 1] limits total debt backed by that collateral inside a group. borrow_limit_outside_elevation_group limits how much of the reserve's own asset can be borrowed by obligations outside any group: the borrow path compares borrow_reserve.borrowed_amount_outside_elevation_group with borrow_reserve.config.borrow_limit_outside_elevation_group.

Save (formerly Solend) separates risk at the pool level. The main pool lists tokens that do not increase risk. Isolated pools hold riskier tokens and are used 'to screen/quarantine them before adding them to the main pool', so an exploit affects only the smaller TVL in that pool. Permissionless pools let anyone create an isolated pool for a fee of 100 SLND; the creator sets the parameters and earns 20% of origination fees. Solend says it does not vet these pools and 'will not be able to compensate users' for bad debt or wrongful liquidations.

Kamino Borrow describes each market (SOL/BTC, JLP, Altcoins, Prime) as a self-contained environment with its own accepted collateral, borrowable assets, risk parameters and liquidity. Collateral in one market cannot back a borrow in another, and markets do not share liquidity or risk exposure, so a liquidation cascade in one market does not touch positions in another.

The tier also sets the oracle confidence multiplier and TWAP sanitization band, from 1x for Collateral to 50x for Isolated and Unlisted.

Drift's spot borrow/lend docs (now at docs.velocity.exchange) describe default accounts as cross-collateralized, with borrows against a volatile token able to socialize bad debt across depositors. They describe isolated pools as a pool subaccount whose deposits and borrows stay within the pool's markets and whose losses cannot reach holdings outside it. The MarginFi (P0) program has exactly two risk tiers, Collateral and Isolated. Bank config validation rejects an Isolated bank unless both its initial and maintenance asset weights are zero, and the health calculation values Isolated-tier deposits at zero. An Isolated bank can still earn interest and be borrowed. A third-party decoder generated from the program's IDL (carbon-marginfi-v2-decoder 2.0.0) lists the same two variants.

Kamino's asset-risk page gives only illustrative LTV bands: low-risk assets might get a Max LTV of 80-85%, and a higher-risk token 50-65% or isolated-mode-only. It publishes no cap numbers and says caps may be reduced on reassessment, so live values must be read from on-chain reserve config.

Kamino documents a permissioned-market feature built on a separate kperm program: it stores a per-market, per-user allowlist, gates DEPOSIT, BORROW, LIQUIDATE and KEYRING actions, requires a kperm co-signature that klend checks on-chain, and never gates withdraw or repay. It is an access control, not a risk tier.

Save's permissionless-pool risk page warns that isolation protects other pools, not a pool's own depositors: a newly listed token can drain the pool through an exploit or team minting even when a depositor only supplies USDC, and thin collateral liquidity can leave bad debt. The page does not say how pools are walled off from each other.

Kamino positions default to Cross Mode: one position can hold several collateral and several debt assets, and LTV is computed over the whole basket. Docs say Cross Mode applies more conservative LTV parameters than Isolated Mode, and that Isolated Mode is a restricted mode for elevated-risk assets that ring-fences the position from the user's other positions.

A December 2025 academic draft on curated lending vaults argues that isolated-by-design structures isolate credit risk more than liquidity risk: 'credit risk remains localized, but liquidity stress is effectively mutualized' when curators route capital through the same underlying markets. It covers Euler, Silo, Morpho and Gearbox-style designs and names no Solana lender, so use it only as a lens for the Jupiter and Kamino dispute.

Kamino's asset-risk and risk-framework pages, read on 2026-11-06, still say every token is placed in General Asset, Isolated Collateral or Isolated Debt, and that Isolated Collateral works only in isolated mode. The program dropped those tiers in release 1.12.7 (2025-11-21), almost a year earlier. Treat that tier language as a policy description, not an on-chain rule, until a current reserve config shows how the restriction is enforced.

In May 2022 a Solend explainer reported six live isolated pools, each with its own assets, risk settings and liquidation rules, defined them as 'independent markets for lending and borrowing', and said Solend then had no public permissionless pool creation. It also warned that users of a breached pool would still take losses. Current Save docs describe permissionless creation, so the 2022 description is out of date.

Mango v4's stable price follows the oracle price but its relative rate of change is limited (stable_growth_limit) and reduced further when it diverges from a 24-hour-delayed 'delay price'. The health code uses min(oracle, stable) for assets and max(oracle, stable) for liabilities in initial health only, so a sudden oracle jump cannot immediately raise borrowing power; maintenance and liquidation health use the plain oracle. The mango-v4 repository was last pushed 2025-04-01 and is not archived; its current mainnet status was not checked.

Velocity's docs say no isolated pool has been deployed on the exchange yet (read 2026-11-06); which pools exist is admin-set onchain state, shown on the borrow and lend page. Isolated-pool accounts cannot place perpetual orders, settle PnL or act as fillers or liquidators, but a pool 0 liquidator can liquidate them. In a bankruptcy the pool's debt is written off against the market's revenue pool, the insurance fund and finally the pool's own depositors. Isolated and main accounts still share one wallet and authority, so operational risk is not isolated.

MarginFi enforces the isolated borrow limit in check_account_risk_tiers: the check passes only if the account has no Isolated-tier liability or exactly one liability in total. Otherwise it fails with IsolatedAccountIllegalState (error 6029, 'Account can have only one liability when account is under isolated risk'). An Isolated borrow therefore must be the account's only borrow. The check runs inside check_account_health, which returns early while the ACCOUNT_IN_FLASHLOAN flag is set, so it is not evaluated mid-flashloan.

Kamino positions default to Cross Mode: one position can hold several collateral and several debt assets, and health is computed over the whole basket under more conservative parameters. Isolated Mode needs exactly one collateral asset and one debt asset and is open only to eligible pairs; the page lists SOL/PYUSD, USDC/USDT and LST/SOL pairs in the SOL/BTC Market, labelled Beta, with more to be added. Kamino says Isolated Mode gives 'enhanced borrow capacity' and 'less restrictive risk parameters' than Cross Mode, and switching back to Cross is free if Cross Mode has enough liquidity.

Pyth's integrator guidance: each price comes with a confidence interval because there is no single price; use the interval bounds (lower bound against downward manipulation, upper against upward), or an EMA, or pause price-dependent activity when confidence/price is wide. Pyth verification does not check an update's age, so the integrating program must enforce its own freshness limit. Pyth gives no numeric confidence threshold.

In MarginFi, an account with a liability on any Isolated-tier bank must have exactly one liability in total. Otherwise the check fails with IsolatedAccountIllegalState (6029, 'Account can have only one liability when account is under isolated risk'). The type crate's comment gives the example that a user can borrow isolated asset XYZ against USDC but not together with SOL. The README's wording, 'Accounts can only borrow one Isolated asset at a time', understates the rule.

In a Velocity isolated pool the loss path is contained: a bankrupt pool subaccount writes its debt off against the market's revenue pool, the insurance fund and finally the pool's own depositors, and balances in pool 0 are never part of that estate. Operational risk is not isolated because both accounts share one wallet and authority. The cost is capital efficiency: neither balance can support the other.

The Oct 2023 Kamino litepaper's tier rules: Isolated Debt assets can be borrowed only in isolation from other assets and cannot be collateral; Isolated Collateral can be used only as collateral and in isolation, and Isolated Debt assets cannot be borrowed against it; General assets can be collateral and be borrowed alongside other General assets. The Risk Council assigns tiers. The tier text was a planned feature at publication.

Velocity (formerly Drift) implements isolated pools with a pool_id on every user and every spot market. The margin calculation fails with InvalidPoolId ('Invalid pool id') when they differ, so one account cannot hold positions across two pools; pool 0 is the main cross-collateralized pool. One exception: a pool 1 user may hold a non-borrow position in spot market 0, whose value the margin code skips. The public protocol-v2 source and the Velocity docs agree on this.

Omnipair describes itself as an oracle-less, isolated-collateral lending and margin-trading protocol on Solana that serves long-tail assets 'without whitelists, external oracles, or centralized risk controls'. Velocity separates the asset tier from isolated pools. Every account and spot market carries a pool id: pool 0 is the main cross-collateralized pool, any other id is an isolated pool, and the margin calculation rejects an account holding positions across two pools. Pool subaccounts can deposit, borrow, repay and swap inside the pool but cannot place perp orders, settle perp P&L or act as filler or liquidator; a pool 0 liquidator can still liquidate them. The docs state that no isolated pool has been deployed on the exchange yet (read 2026-11-06).

A Reference Price Check blocks an update or reverts the transaction when a refreshed price differs from its reference by more than a tolerance (default 5%).

MarginFi isolates by configuration rather than by separate pools. A Group is a set of Banks under one admin, typically a governance multisig, with delegate admins for narrower changes. Each Bank holds one asset's weights, oracle, interest curve, risk tier and operational state, and many Banks can exist for one asset. An Account belongs to one Group, holds up to 16 Balances, and its health is the sum of weighted assets minus weighted liabilities across all of them, so ordinary banks are cross-collateral inside an account.

Scope supports entry types beyond a plain feed. MostRecentOf returns the freshest of up to four sources and fails, rather than picking one, if any source is stale or the high-low spread exceeds a configured tolerance. CappedFloored clamps a source price to a ceiling, a floor or both. CappedMostRecentOf adds an upper bound to MostRecentOf. DiscountToMaturity accretes linearly to par at a set maturity date, for PT tokens, T-bills and similar assets. SplStake reads a stake pool's redemption rate. Save (formerly Solend) prices each reserve with four u8 percent parameters: optimal_utilization_rate, min_borrow_rate, optimal_borrow_rate and max_borrow_rate. current_borrow_rate is linear on each leg. Below the optimum, rate = min + (U / U_opt) x (optimal - min). At or above it, rate = optimal + ((U - U_opt) / (1 - U_opt)) x (max - optimal). If optimal_utilization_rate = 100 the first leg is used throughout. The integration-guide TypeScript implements the same two legs.

DefiLlama's lending-pool 'tvlUsd' is liquidity not lent out, not total deposits. The P0 adaptor comments 'Pool TVL = liquidity not lent out (DefiLlama lending convention)', the Save adaptor labels it 'available liquidity', and the Jupiter vault adaptor sets tvlUsd = supply minus borrow. So Save's SOL pool shows $7.74M of TVL against $18.46M supplied and $10.71M borrowed, and Kamino's SOL/BTC Market SOL pool shows $19.74M against $216.6M supplied. Take supply and borrow totals from lendBorrow (totalSupplyUsd, totalBorrowUsd), not from tvlUsd.

Scope prices on-chain are copies that crankers refresh. They are not fetched at transaction time. Kamino says it runs multiple independent crankers that push Scope updates, and its developer docs call the refresh instruction permissionless, with leverage and flash-loan flows commonly including a refresh before execution. Project 0's docs say the feed operator refreshes Scope entries, a caller has nothing to crank, and each bank's oracle_max_age applies to the entry's own timestamp.

marginfi's handle_bankruptcy settles an account whose liabilities remain after all its assets are liquidated. In order: the bank's insurance vault pays min(bad debt, vault balance). The remainder is socialized by lowering the bank's asset share value, which cuts every depositor's balance pro rata. If the remainder is at least the bank's total asset value, the share value goes to zero and the bank is set to KilledByBankruptcy, which is irreversible. Only the group admin or risk_admin may call it unless the bank has PERMISSIONLESS_BAD_DEBT_SETTLEMENT_FLAG.

Kamino computes utilization as borrowed / total_supply, where total_supply = available + borrowed - accumulated protocol fees - accumulated referrer fees - pending referrer fees. That is slightly higher than borrowed / (available + borrowed). The lender rate is utilization x curve borrow rate x (1 - protocol_take_rate_pct / 100). Kamino's docs write the same rule as S = U x B x (1 - R), and the SDK's calculateSupplyAPR implements it.

Kamino's own pages say Scope has processed $19.33B of volume with zero oracle-related exploits, was audited by Sec3 (16 Dec 2024), OtterSec (16 Dec 2023) and Offside Labs (8 Dec 2023), that the Multi-Price Oracle System was double-audited by Certora and Offside Labs, and that a February 2026 stress event produced 55,649 liquidation events across 30,030 wallets in 48 hours with zero bad debt. These are Kamino's figures and were not independently checked.

Kamino's app 'Isolated Mode' is documented as one collateral asset and one debt asset per position, limited to listed pairs (as of beta: SOL/PYUSD, USDC/USDT and LST/SOL, all in the SOL/BTC Market). The on-chain groups (single debt reserve, mostly one collateral reserve, PYUSD, USDC, USDT and SOL debt) fit that description, but no Kamino page says Isolated Mode is implemented as an elevation group.

Save accrues per slot: slot_rate = borrow_rate / SLOTS_PER_YEAR, compounded = (1 + slot_rate)^slots_elapsed, applied to cumulative_borrow_rate and borrowed_amount at each reserve refresh. The reserve config comments call min, optimal and max 'borrow APY', but the program treats them as nominal annual rates compounded per slot, so the effective yearly rate is above the stated number. Save's APY page says the displayed APY compounds over a year and that borrow interest is added per slot.

Kamino's docs index describes Lending Vaults as 'Single-token managed yield aggregation across Kamino's lending markets', and the allocation page's worked examples put reserves from the SOL/BTC, JLP and Altcoin markets in one vault with weights and per-reserve caps. Market isolation therefore bounds a borrower's position inside one market, while a vault depositor can hold exposure to several markets through one vault. A curator can restrict a vault to whitelisted reserves.

handle_bankruptcy also refuses durable-nonce transactions, accounts inside a flash loan, and accounts in receivership liquidation. It writes off any uncollectable premium receivable without crediting lenders, then disables the account and sets has_been_bankrupted. This is the on-chain guard against settling a transiently insolvent account.

Drift gave a structural reason for not paying its remaining assets back to lenders directly: all its borrow and lend markets share one liquidity pool, so returning deposits before borrows are repaid would remove liquidity other accounts depend on and break the pool's accounting. It chose to convert the remaining assets (about $3.8M at the time) to stablecoin and back the recovery token instead.

Project 0 and Kamino price principal tokens (PTs) and similar fixed-maturity assets by modelled accretion to par, not market price. Project 0's PTPyth and PTFixed setups multiply a base by a linear rate that rises from a configured start price to par at the vault's maturity, capped by what the PT can redeem for. Kamino's DiscountToMaturity applies an annual discount rate in basis points so the price climbs linearly to exactly 1.0 at the maturity timestamp.

Source types: Pyth, Chainlink, Redstone, StakePool (e.g. Jito), MsolPool, SinglePool (3 accounts) and JupLend fToken rate (4 accounts). Mango Markets, Oct 2022 (a Solana margin and perps venue with lending pools): the exploiter inflated MNGO's price, borrowed against unrealized perp profit and drained the borrow liquidity. That left about a $115M shortfall (bad debt) in his account while the treasury held about $70M. marginfi accrues interest as simple (non-compounded) growth per update interval: new share value = value x (1 + apr x time_delta / SECONDS_PER_YEAR). Compounding therefore happens only through repeated updates, so a quoted APR and the realised APY differ with update frequency.

marginfi puts its fees on the borrower side. Lending APR = base rate x utilization, with no fee deduction. Borrowing APR = base x (1 + insurance_ir_fee + group_ir_fee + program_fee_rate) + fixed fee APRs (insurance, group, program). The program fee applies only if the group enables it. Fee APRs are collected on total liabilities and reported separately, so the borrow-lend spread = (1 - utilization) x base + base x rate fees + fixed fees.

Jupiter Lend's @jup-ag/lend-read Liquidity module returns supplyRate, borrowRate and lastStoredUtilization in basis points (divide by 100 for percent), and calculateExchangePrice(config) projects exchange prices to now. The docs call the rates APYs in prose and name the converted variables supplyApr and borrowApr. The program stores borrow_rate as a nominal annual rate in 1e2 units and grows exchange prices linearly per second between updates, so treat the values as APR-like, not as compounded APY.

On 23 May 2025 Judge Arun Subramanian vacated all of Eisenberg's April 2024 criminal convictions (commodities fraud, commodities manipulation, wire fraud). TRM Labs reports the commodities counts fell on venue (he traded from Puerto Rico), the wire fraud count fell on venue and for lack of a material misrepresentation, and the court still found sufficient evidence of a manipulative device. The Block quotes the judge: 'On a platform with no rules, instructions, or prohibitions about borrowing, the government needed more'. This scopes the 'oracle manipulation equals fraud' framing: the wire frau

Save's market-config API adds userSupplyCap and userBorrowCap to some main-pool reserves (SOL 1,000,000 / 2,000,000; USDC 30,000,000 / 50,000,000) and omits them for JitoSOL. They are not the on-chain depositLimit and borrowLimit (SOL 1,000,000 / 200,000 SOL; USDC 75,000,000 / 25,000,000). Their units are undocumented and I found no program code that enforces them.

Save's market-config API exposes userSupplyCap and userBorrowCap per reserve (SOL 1,000,000 and 2,000,000; USDC 30,000,000 and 50,000,000; none for JitoSOL). They are not the reserve-wide limits: on-chain SOL borrowLimit is 200,000 SOL and USDC depositLimit is 75,000,000. They look like per-user caps, but no source I read defines them, so do not use them as pool caps.

Save (formerly Solend) splits markets into a global main pool, smaller curated isolated pools and permissionless isolated pools. The docs say most TVL sits in the main pool, tokens usually start in isolated pools and move to the main pool after enough time, and isolated pools act as a quarantine so a problem 'will only affect the smaller TVLs' there. A May 2022 explainer describes isolated pools as independent lending and borrowing markets, with six pools and over $660M TVL at the time.

facts.text: Controversy: Sources frame the Mango root cause differently. BankInfoSecurity reports the vulnerability stemmed from thin liquidity in the MNGO/USDC market. Decrypt quotes OtterSec's founder calling it 'an economic design flaw'. Mango's own tweet called it 'an oracle price manipulation'. A statement carried by BankInfoSecurity, with attribution ambiguous between Mango and OtterSec, says 'Neither oracle providers have any fault here. The oracle price reporting worked as it should have'. The SEC press release describes the scheme without mentioning an oracle.

Controversy: Mango Markets, 11 October 2022: Eisenberg put about $5M USDC into two accounts, held both sides of an MNGO perpetual position, then bought thinly traded MNGO spot on the exchanges that fed Mango's oracle (FTX, AscendEX, Serum per TRM Labs). MNGO rose from about $0.03 to $0.91 and the position was valued at about $423M. He borrowed and withdrew about $116M (SEC figure) and the platform was left with a deficit when the price fell back. About $67M was later returned in a DAO-mediated settlement.

Controversy: DefiLlama 'TVL' for Kamino Lend, marginfi, Jupiter Lend and Save is the unborrowed liquidity left in vaults: the adapters sum reserve or bank vault balances and report borrows separately (Save's adapter says 'borrowed tokens are not counted'). Total supplied is therefore roughly TVL plus borrowed. Project 0 is the exception: its adapter reports gross deposits and is flagged doublecounted. Vendor figures follow the deposit basis: Solana Compass quotes Jupiter Lend at '$1.5B TVL' in December 2025, close to DefiLlama's TVL plus borrowed ($1.59B on 2025-12-03) rather than its TVL ($0.99B).
